title: Traffic-bridging and soft-retire procedures for version-locked models
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Background: Customers can pin a model version (version-lock) to guarantee output compatibility. When a pinned model is deprecated, or a regional capacity issue occurs, the platform must bridge traffic to compatible alternatives without breaking customer contracts or surface regressions. Goal: implement a transparent traffic-bridging policy and soft-retirement workflow for version-locked models that preserves SLOs, provides auditability, and minimizes customer-visible regressions. Scope includes routing logic, compatibility checks, telemetry, rollout controls, canary ramps, and operator runbooks. Out of scope: automated model retraining or editing customer prompts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Route-level policy can route traffic from a deprecated version to a compatible variant with configurable ramp (0-100%)
2) Compatibility check: runtime validates model artifact ABI + tokenizer checksum before allowing substitution
3) Per-customer opt-in/opt-out flag respected; default is platform-managed fallback when safety and quality gates pass
4) Telemetry emitted for every substitute decision (reason, source_version, target_version, ramp_pct, region, request_id)
5) Runbook steps for emergency rollback and customer notification exist and are tested in staging
design_decisions: Prefer additive traffic-bridging (weighted routing) over immediate cutover to allow phased detection of regressions
Use a deterministic compatibility fingerprint (model ABI hash + tokenizer hash + static config) to gate substitution; avoid relying solely on semantic evals for admission
Store fallback chains as versioned policy objects in control plane so historical decisions are auditable
Support per-route per-customer overrides via route config (enforced at routing layer)
tradeoffs: Strict fingerprint gating reduces unsafe substitutions but can increase manual work when models are semantically compatible but ABI-changed
Weighted ramps increase exposure time to regressions but provide safer detection and less customer churn
Adding compatibility checks into the runtime adds latency to model selection path (expected 1-3ms), but keeps decision consistent and auditable
rollout_plan: 2) Unit + integration tests + mutation tests in CI
3) Canary in staging across 2 orgs with synthetic workload (2 days)
4) Gradual rollout in production: start 1% across non-SLA orgs -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% (monitor for 24h at each step)
5) Post-rollout audit and opt-in messaging to pinned customers
monitoring_and_alerts: SLA break (latency P99 > target) for routes using traffic-bridge
Quality regression alert: automated evals on canary traffic show > 5% degradation in rubric score
Unexpected substitution rate > X% in a region triggers investigation
Audit-log ingestion failures for policy decisions
implementation_tasks: ENG-56012: control-plane API for fallback-chain CRUD
ENG-56013: runtime gating and fingerprint validator
ENG-56015: Console UI for per-route override and ramp configuration
ENG-56016: E2E tests and staging canary harness
open_questions: Q1: Should we allow heuristic substitution when fingerprint mismatch but semantic evals are within threshold? (security vs. availability)
Q2: What default ramp cadence to expose in Console for non-enterprise customers?
Q3: How to display fallback decisions in audit log for customers without exposing stack internals?
